children: reported lower quarterly profit on Thursday, weighed down by a one-time accounting charge, while revenue hit a record high.

El Al kept its planes mostly full despite competition for passengers from foreign airlines who resumed flights to Tel Aviv after suspending them following the outbreak of the US-Israeli war with Iran.
Third-quarter net profit was $175 million, down from $203 million a year earlier. The decline was largely due to an accounting charge of $24 million from revaluing a phantom option
Revenue rose to $1.27 billion from $1.07 billion, while load factor — the share of seats filled — remained at 95% in the
El Al, Israel's flag carrier, said it had an order backlog of $1.1 billion based on advance sales of tickets, up 16% from a year earlier
Available seat kilometres grew 9% year-over-year, driven by fleet expansion

Given its rapid growth over the past few years, partly due to many foreign airlines halting flights during conflicts in Gaza and with Iran, the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange added El Al to its blue-chip TA-35 index
this week with a valuation of nearly $4 billion
El Al declared a quarterly dividend of $116 million
CEO Levy Halevy said: "By increasing seat capacity while maintaining high load factors, we have achieved one of the strongest periods in the company's history."
